display.title: Episode 337: The Dike (Tisha B'Av)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's show for the week of Tisha B'Av: Torah, Avodah and Gemilus Chasadim, Shema with a first-grader, the story of the Dike, and the ancient tune of Eicha.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Tisha B'Av 5748. Uncle Yossi opens with the teaching of the Sages that the world stands on three things: learning Torah, davening to Hashem, and acts of kindness, especially tzedakah, the best 'diet' for a healthy neshamah. A first-grade yeshivah boy then leads the Shema in Studio 604. Story time is 'The Dike': when the dike breaks in a Dutch seaside town, little Gittel falls behind the fleeing crowd and is taken in by a harsh old woman who works her hard and makes her forget her family and her Yiddishkeit. Years later, Shabbos candles glowing in a window bring back her memories and lead her home to her parents and sister. Next, Uncle Yossi speaks about music as a gift from Hashem and introduces the age-old tune of Eicha, a song of hope sung throughout the golus. He explains why this year's fast is postponed from Shabbos to Sunday, how Tisha B'Av begins right after Shabbos, and prays that it become a Yom Tov. The show ends with the Shabbos candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Torah, davening and kindness keep the neshamah strong; and the light of Shabbos candles can bring a lost Jewish child back home.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: 'this coming Shabbos is Tisha B'Av', fast postponed to Sunday; candle time given for Friday, July 22nd.

advisories.note: A lost girl is kept for three years by a cruel woman who forbids her to mention her family and works her hard.
A dike breaks and a town flees the flood; a child is threatened with a beating.
Tisha B'Av and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash, explained gently.

sources_cited.note: Cited as 'our Chachamim tell us': the world stands on Torah, Avodah and Gemilus Chasadim.
Cited as 'our Chachamim': 'Az Yashir' in the future tense hints at the song of the Geulah.
Cited loosely as the Rambam: turn only to Hashem for whatever you need.
